A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 20 readable pages, including Appendices A–F. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and image-classification unlearning experiments in Section 5, with additional results and uncertainty reporting in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and outcomes in Section 5 and Appendix F, including Tables 1–9 and Figures 1–4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the surrogate Hessian estimate, Newton update, and calibrated Gaussian noise. The classifier-based KL approximation, SGLD sampling, and variational estimation procedures are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic Gaussian data, CIFAR-10, StanfordDogs, Caltech256, and MNIST–USPS experiments. Random-sample forgetting, class forgetting, and cross-dataset surrogate scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Retrain, Unlearn (+), and Unlearn (-), with Original additionally reported in Appendix F. Ahmed et al. (2025) is newly discussed but is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, distribution-parameter sweeps, forget ratios, model configurations, and accuracy/MIA/RT/forget-score metrics are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same privacy parameters, regularization, sampling settings, and estimator training procedure.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the distribution-distance, forget-ratio, and architecture analyses. Appendix F contains the same comparisons of heuristic KL and unlearning-error estimates against exact or reference quantities.

E5.justification: Both versions already describe multiple trials with different seeds and report error bars and table error margins in Appendix F. No run-count information or uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain identical numerical entries, and Figures 1–4 use identical plot images. Reported accuracy, forgetting, noise, KL-divergence, and bound-estimation findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, bounds, and proofs in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–D are unchanged. v2's references to items such as Assumption 4.1 as 'Theorem 4.1' are labeling inconsistencies, not mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows 'no theoretical guarantees exist' to 'no theoretical guarantees on certified unlearning exist.' This refines the research-gap claim; the abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of noise calibration, utility preservation, and heuristic KL estimation remain unchanged. Both versions retain the qualifications concerning approximate certification, convexity assumptions, and membership-inference evaluation for class forgetting.

D1.justification: The Software section changes the mixed-linear-network repository destination from info-ucr/mixed-privacy-forgetting to info-ucr/source-free-unlearning. The main implementation link and Appendix E details remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the replacement repository's contents or availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ahmed et al. (2025), 'Towards Source-Free Machine Unlearning,' to the introduction, related work, and bibliography. It distinguishes that concurrent work's methodological bounds from formal certified guarantees. Previously cited works remain.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work section receive localized additions. Appendix references become Section references, while numerous references to assumptions, definitions, lemmas, corollaries, and propositions incorrectly become Theorem references. The overall organization is retained.

P2.justification: Text additions and reference edits produce localized column and bibliography reflow, particularly on pages 3–4 and 10–11. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–9 retain their displays, captions, numbering, and placement.

improvement.justification: The added concurrent-work discussion and narrower research-gap statement improve attribution and precision. However, v2 introduces systematic cross-reference mislabeling, and the changed code link's practical effect cannot be established from the PDFs. With the method, mathematics, and empirical evidence unchanged, these opposing editorial effects do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
